title: Managers Who Quit Soon After Promotion
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article opens with a striking statistic: more than 20 percent of newly promoted managers leave their organization within six months. The author explains this counterintuitive trend by pointing to a lack of structured support during the vulnerable transition period, when newly promoted leaders face unfamiliar challenges without a mentor to help them navigate. The piece notes that organizations often assume someone deemed ready for promotion shouldn't need extra help, which is precisely the wrong assumption. It also acknowledges promotions can sometimes come too late or simply flag a rising employee to outside recruiters. The core recommendation is that organizations should pair every promotion with deliberate resources and support rather than treating the title change as sufficient on its own.
points: More than 20 percent of newly promoted managers leave their organization within six months of promotion.
The leading explanation is inadequate organizational support during the vulnerable early transition period.
Organizations often wrongly assume that a person ready for promotion needs no additional help.
The newly promoted need mentorship and resources from day one, not just the title change itself.
Pairing every promotion with real support is framed as an easy, high-leverage fix for retention.
quotes: Within six months of being promoted, more than 20 percent of new leaders and managers quit.
In essence, they celebrate their promotion by finding another role somewhere else.
Feeling new to a role is hard enough, but when a manager feels left to fend for themselves in the face of ambiguity, they sometimes jump ship.
The newly promoted are in need of resources, training, and support from day one.
The best organizations offer two rewards together: the promotion and the support the newly-promoted team member needs to succeed.
As it turns out, newly-promoted managers and leaders abandon ship if they don’t have the resources and support they need to succeed.
